questions.q: What are this lesson's two example data sources?
options: Two separate CSV files
orders.csv and a live AdventureWorks2012 database query
Two REST APIs
A JSON file and an Excel file
questions.explain: One extract function reads orders.csv; the other queries Production.ProductCategory over pyodbc.

questions.q: Why does extract_all() return a dictionary instead of a single combined DataFrame?
options: Dictionaries are required by pandas
So the Transform stage can pull out exactly the source it needs by name, and new sources can be added as new keys
A DataFrame cannot hold more than one source's data
It has no real benefit over a single DataFrame
questions.explain: Keying by source name lets the pipeline scale to more sources without restructuring the return value.

questions.q: Why is it intentional that orders.csv and Production.ProductCategory are unrelated datasets in this lesson?
options: Because the lesson is demonstrating the extract-per-source pattern itself, not a join between the two
Because AdventureWorks2012 cannot be joined to any CSV data
It's a mistake that should be fixed
Because pandas cannot combine data from two different sources
questions.explain: The point is that each source gets its own extract function, regardless of whether the sources relate to each other.

questions.q: In the error-handling version of extract_all(), what happens if extract_product_categories() raises a pyodbc.Error?
options: The entire script crashes immediately with no message
orders.csv also fails to load
The error is logged, that source is set to None, and the orders data still loads successfully
The function retries the database connection forever
questions.explain: The try/except around just that source means a database outage doesn't block the still-usable CSV data.

questions.q: What does extract_product_categories() use to pull data from AdventureWorks2012?
options: A plain text file reader
pyodbc to connect, and pd.read_sql() to return a DataFrame
The requests library
A hardcoded Python list
questions.explain: It reuses Chapter 5's pyodbc connection and pd.read_sql() pattern for a real database source.
